The refresher still runs one read per connector and scope at a time, but a request that arrives during a read is now remembered and run once that read ends, with the env as it is then, so a branch change reads the new branch and a push gets its read. Several requests during one read merge into one rerun, which goes back through the usual checks; `stop()` drops pending reruns.

good call. I measured it in local runs..

An idle toggle flips in about 85ms, same as main. The switch only waits if you click it while a session is still being set up: right after another switch, right after sending a new task’s first message, or right after resuming a task from history. How long it waits is almost entirely the remote-config fetch every session start does:
- fast API: a rebuild takes about 300ms
- API delayed 1.5s: about 1.8s
- API unresponsive: the fetch waits out its 10s timeout, so a rebuild takes about 10.3s, and a toggle landing mid-rebuild sat unflipped for 6.3s in my run

I tried to play with other factors (repo size, a hundred rules, skills and workflows, long transcripts and MCP), and they barely moved it.

For comparison, those same three moments are exactly when main breaks. The switch flips instantly, but the session ends up in the other mode. A slow API makes that more likely in exactly the cases where this PR waits longer.

So **yes, the “stuck” switch is real on slow networks**. But I think the inconsistent state is the bigger problem. It’s silent, it doesn’t heal on its own (toggling back and forth didn’t help the reporter), and it costs the user real work. The stuck switch is visible, ends on its own, and is safe: clicking again just asks for the same mode, and anything sent meanwhile waits and runs in the mode you end up seeing.

For the toggle itself, we could do this as a follow-up:
1. Flip the switch immediately with a pending state (dimmed slider or a “Switching to Act…” tooltip), and flip it back with a short explanation if the switch fails. Maybe a notification only if the wait gets long, so it doesn’t nag on every slow toggle
2. Coalesce rapid toggles, so Plan then Act before the first rebuild starts only rebuilds once

+// SdkCloudSessionCoordinator — starts, reopens and monitors Cline Cloud sessions.
+//
+// Cloud sessions run in a hosted sandbox and keep going after the user moves on,
+// so this coordinator owns two things the local task flow does not need:
+//
+//   1. A registry of live sandbox connections (CloudSessionHost). A connection
+//      is kept after the user leaves the task view so the agent's real status
+//      (running / completed / failed) stays known for History and so a
+//      background cloud task can raise a "finished" notification. REST alone
+//      cannot tell a busy agent from an idle sandbox ("active" only means the
+//      sandbox is up).
+//   2. The projection of cloud records into task history (SessionHistoryRecord
+//      shape) so History, the home screen and the running-now strip list cloud
+//      tasks next to local ones.

+		if (this.scopeTransition || this.disposed) return

+			return this.listPromise
+		}

+		let listPromise!: Promise<void>

+			try {

+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) {
+					return
+				}

+			} finally {

+				}
+			}

+		return listPromise
+	}

+			}
+			return existing

+			pinned: 0,

+			lastActivityAt: Date.parse(record.updatedAt) || Date.now(),
+		}

+		return entry
+	}

+		this.scopeGeneration++
+		this.statusResolutionAttempts.clear()
+		const previousTransition = this.scopeTransition
+		const transition = (async () => {
+			await previousTransition
+			this.listFetchedAt = 0
+			this.listPromise = undefined
+			if (this.pollTimer) {
+				clearInterval(this.pollTimer)
+				this.pollTimer = undefined
+			}
+			if (this.options.getTask()?.taskId && isCloudSessionId(this.options.getTask()?.taskId)) {
+				await this.options.clearTask()
+			}
+			const entries = [...this.entries.values()]
+			const hosts = entries.flatMap((entry) => (entry.host ? [entry.host] : []))
+			const connections = entries.flatMap((entry) => (entry.connection ? [entry.connection] : []))
+			this.entries.clear()
+			this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+			// Starts and deletions own their cleanup until settlement. Keep the originating
+			// account active through every await, including DELETE; never retain old tokens.
+			void this.trackScopeOperation(() =>
+				Promise.allSettled([...connections, ...hosts.map((host) => host.dispose("accountScopeChanged"))]),
+			)
+			await this.drainScopeOperations([...this.scopeOperations])
+			await changeScope?.()
+		})()
+		this.scopeTransition = transition
+		try {
+			await transition
+		} finally {
+			if (this.scopeTransition === transition) {
+				this.scopeTransition = undefined
+				// Refresh even after failure: the server may have switched accounts
+				// before a later auth/config refresh failed.
+				if (!this.disposed) {
+					this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+					void this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}

+	private trackScopeOperation<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
+		// Enroll before executing any code that can yield or re-enter reset.
+		const promise = Promise.resolve().then(operation)
+		this.scopeOperations.add(promise)
+		return promise.finally(() => this.scopeOperations.delete(promise))
+	}

+	private async drainScopeOperations(operations: Promise<unknown>[]): Promise<void> {
+		let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
+		try {
+			await Promise.race([
+				Promise.allSettled(operations),
+				new Promise<never>((_resolve, reject) => {
+					timer = setTimeout(
+						() =>
+							reject(
+								new Error(
+									"Cloud session cleanup is still pending. Your account has not changed; try again after cleanup finishes.",
+								),
+							),
+						SCOPE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS,
+					)
+				}),
+			])
+		} finally {
+			clearTimeout(timer)
+		}
+	}

+			if (entry.record === record) {
+				entry.agentStatus = status
+				if (isSettled(status)) this.rememberStatus(record, status, Date.now())
+			}
+			this.ensurePolling()
+			return host
+		})()
+		entry.connection = connection
+		try {
+			return await connection
+		} finally {
+			if (entry.connection === connection) entry.connection = undefined
+		}
+	}
+
+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+		if (!entry) {
+			return
+		}
+		const previous = entry.agentStatus
+		const now = Date.now()
+		entry.agentStatus = status
+		if (isSettled(status)) {
+			this.rememberStatus(entry.record, status, now)
+		}
+		// Learning the current status on connect is not agent activity; only a
+		// change observed while connected moves the task up in History.
+		if (previous !== undefined && previous !== status) {
+			entry.lastActivityAt = now
+		}
+		this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+		const isDisplayed = this.options.getTask()?.taskId === sessionId
+		if (!isDisplayed && previous !== undefined && previous !== status && (status === "completed" || status === "failed")) {
+			this.notifyFinished(entry, status)
+		}
+		this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+	}
+
+	private notifyFinished(entry: CloudSessionEntry, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const title = entry.title ?? entry.record.title?.trim() ?? entry.record.repoContext.repoUrl ?? entry.record.id
+		const label = status === "failed" ? "Cloud task failed" : "Cloud task finished"
+		HostProvider.window
+			.showMessage({
+				type: status === "failed" ? ShowMessageType.WARNING : ShowMessageType.INFORMATION,
+				message: `${label}: ${title}`,
+				options: { items: ["Open"] },
+			})
+			.then((response) => {
+				if (!this.disposed && this.entries.get(entry.record.id) === entry && response.selectedOption === "Open") {
+					return this.openCloudTask(entry.record.id)
+				}
+				return undefined
+			})
+			.catch((error) => Logger.warn("[CloudSessions] Failed to show completion notification:", error))
+	}
+
+	private ensurePolling(): void {
+		if (this.pollTimer || this.disposed) {
+			return
+		}
+		this.pollTimer = setInterval(() => void this.pollTick(), ACTIVE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS)
+		this.pollTimer.unref?.()
+	}
+
+	private async pollTick(): Promise<void> {
+		if (this.disposed) {
+			return
+		}
+		const now = Date.now()
+		for (const entry of this.entries.values()) {
+			const status = this.statusOf(entry)
+			if (
+				entry.host &&
+				!this.isHostInUse(entry) &&
+				!ACTIVE_CLOUD_STATUSES.has(status) &&
+				// Loss of observation is not evidence that the sandbox stopped.
+				status !== "unknown" &&
+				now - entry.lastActivityAt > IDLE_CONNECTION_TTL_MS
+			) {
+				// Finished a while ago and nobody is looking: release the socket.
+				await entry.host.dispose("idle").catch(() => undefined)
+				entry.host = undefined
+			}
+		}
+		const hasActive = [...this.entries.values()].some((entry) => ACTIVE_CLOUD_STATUSES.has(this.statusOf(entry)))
+		if (hasActive || this.entries.size > 0) {
+			await this.refreshList(true)
+			this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+			this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+		}
+		if (![...this.entries.values()].some((entry) => entry.host)) {
+			clearInterval(this.pollTimer)
+			this.pollTimer = undefined
+		}
+	}
+
+	// ---- Starting a task ----
+
+	/**
+	 * The Cline model a new sandbox runs: the user's Act-mode Cline model,
+	 * else the top recommendation known so far. Synchronous, and the only
+	 * source for both the composer label and the start path, so the sandbox
+	 * runs the model the user saw when they submitted.
+	 */
+	private nextCloudModelId(): string {
+		const apiConfig = this.options.stateManager.getApiConfiguration()
+		if (apiConfig.actModeApiProvider === "cline" && apiConfig.actModeClineModelId?.trim()) {
+			return apiConfig.actModeClineModelId.trim()
+		}
+		this.warmRecommendedModels()
+		const recommended = getCachedClineRecommendedModels() ?? CLINE_RECOMMENDED_MODELS_FALLBACK
+		return recommended.recommended[0]?.id ?? CLINE_RECOMMENDED_MODELS_FALLBACK.recommended[0].id
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * Fetches the recommendation list so the composer label moves from the
+	 * built-in fallback to the live recommendation before the user submits.
+	 * State is re-posted when the list lands. A fetch that fails to populate
+	 * the cache releases the handle, so the next state post retries instead of
+	 * pinning the fallback until restart.
+	 */
+	private warmRecommendedModels(): void {
+		if (this.recommendedModelsWarmup || getCachedClineRecommendedModels()) {
+			return
+		}
+		const warmup = refreshClineRecommendedModels()
+			.then(() => {
+				if (!this.disposed) this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+			})
+			.catch(() => undefined)
+			.finally(() => {
+				if (this.recommendedModelsWarmup === warmup) {

The warm-up now posts state only when the fetch filled the cache; a fetch that returned the fallback releases the handle without posting, so the next read the user causes retries but nothing loops on its own. The test asserts no state post after the failed fetch and exactly one after the successful retry.

Fixed in 4e4d602c4. The PUT is now always sent (matching what main does for the ClinePass path), so an account another client moved is restored. Only the cloud teardown is gated on the cached account actually changing, since that is what scoped the cloud state. `account-service.test.ts` "restores the server account without tearing down cloud state when the cached account already matches" covers it.

This is inherent in the distributed nature of the system and is a gap we can only narrow but not close in the current design. We will accept this limitation for now. If an error arises, it probably relates to something the user did recently, and the recovery path is pretty straightforward: Switch organizations and try the operation again. Not to mention, only a few users have organizations.

Implemented in `84db143`.

The response is claimed before the first asynchronous delivery step, so a second submission cannot resolve the same question. It is routed through the normal follow-up path while the claimed response continues delivering its attachments. I kept the session identity check and retained a per-attempt validity token so cancellation, replacement questions, delivery failures, and retries remain safe: an old callback cannot become current again after a retry, and a failed attempt releases only its own claim.

The focused VS Code suites cover the overlap, cancellation, failure/retry, and stale-callback cases and pass; SDK typecheck also passes. The separate display fix keeps the original pending-question text in the submitted event while preserving the expanded model prompt.

Implemented in commit `84db143`.

The pending ask response is now claimed synchronously before attachment preparation begins. While that claim is in flight, another submission cannot resolve the same `ask_question`; it falls through to the normal follow-up path instead. The claim is tied to the individual delivery attempt, so cancellation or replacement of the question invalidates older callbacks, while a delivery error releases only its own claim and leaves the original response retryable.

I added regressions covering overlapping text and attachment submissions, cancellation during delivery, delivery failure followed by a retry, and stale `isCurrent` callbacks after a replacement question. The focused VS Code suites pass (231 tests total), and the SDK typecheck passes.

Valid, fixed in ffb6b03bd3. Each session copy now records the generation (import) it came from, and `isUsable` checks that copy's own generation instead of comparing against the entry's current one. `reload` starts a new generation and leaves older copies callable, which is what its doc says. Failure counts and blocking are per generation: a broken reload cannot turn off copies that still work, and failures in an old copy are logged and reported to the sessions running it but do not change the status, which always describes the current generation. One deliberate exception: an uncaught error attributed by stack turns off every live generation, because a stack cannot tell copies of the same file apart (fails closed). Tests: "keeps running sessions' copies usable across a reload" and "does not let a broken reload turn off copies that still work".

Good catch, fixed in 98d674cfa. shutdownSession now deletes the slot only when it still points at the runtime being shut down, the same guard releaseSessionRuntime already had. Regression test: a stop stalled in the resident's agent shutdown while a same-id start registers the replacement; the replacement stays reachable afterwards (fails with session_not_found without the guard).

Valid, fixed in a65115d1c. The pending-start entry in sessionStarts now records an abort issued while the start is in flight; a turn that waited on that start completes as aborted (done event, aborted result) without running on the replacement. The agent runtime ignores an abort before run() starts, so this has to be decided at the host before the turn is dispatched. Regression test: B sends during A's rebuild, aborts before it finishes, the turn resolves aborted with neither agent's run called, and the replacement takes the next turn normally.

With efd698c2e the release runs after the replacement is already live, so failing the caller's start would report an error for a session that is working. releaseSessionRuntime logs each stage failure and captures it to telemetry before rethrowing, so nothing is lost by swallowing it at this call site.

Fixed in 17ff65c7b. The old runtime is now released in a finally, so it is torn down whether the rebuild resolves or throws (including the case where the replacement claimed the slot and then its initial turn failed and removed it). The release guard only deletes the map entry when it still points at the old object, so a live replacement is left in place; a failed rebuild leaves no resident, and the next start rebuilds from disk. Test updated to assert the resident is released (not stranded) when the rebuild's build throws.

`request()` coalesces a newer request into `pending`, but it doesn't invalidate an already-active rebuild for the same reason — `cancellationGeneration` only moves in `cancel()` (line 40). So the active run's `isCurrent()` stays `true`, and once it finishes the newer request rebuilds the session again.

There's a correctness window here, not just redundant work. If the active rebuild has already snapshotted its config when the newer setting arrives, it installs the superseded one; and for checkpoint rebuilds it can replay a deferred follow-up from the shared `checkpointTransition` before the newer rebuild applies the latest setting — so a real message can run under the old checkpoint config.

I don't think bumping the generation here is a self-contained fix: the transition object is shared between the active and queued requests, and an invalidated rebuild returning from `replaceActiveSession()` can still clear `this.checkpointTransition` and stop the replacement. Either make a same-reason request explicitly supersede the active run with the transition ownership handled to match, or rename `isCurrent()` so it's clear it only means "not cancelled". A scheduler test for requesting a reason while that reason is actively rebuilding would pin whichever contract you pick.

Thanks — you were right on both counts, and the second one hid a real defect.

`isCurrent()` in a78223a means exactly "no newer request for the same reason has arrived": `request()` stamps a per-reason generation, and a running rebuild's context reads it live. `cancel()` and the per-reason cancellation generation are gone; nothing could reach them because `runTaskTransition` waits for the drain first.

The shared `checkpointTransition` is gone too. Holding a follow-up outside Core's queue meant nothing rendered it: a message typed during a turn after toggling Checkpoints vanished from the chat until the turn ended (this is what the e2e was failing on across all three CI platforms). Follow-ups now always go to Core's queue. The scheduler treats a session with queued prompts as busy, since Core drains the queue the instant a turn ends, and a send that settles after Core already started the next queued turn no longer flips the session idle. There is a scheduler test for a same-reason request during an active rebuild, and coordinator tests for supersession before replacement.

Valid, thanks. Fixed in cd3582cca: host replacement now chains onto the previous host promise so concurrent callers serialize, and a stale host is shut down and reloaded exactly once. Verified against the real goal plugin: three concurrent cold calls spawned one sandbox, and two concurrent calls after bumping the plugin mtime replaced it once with no leaked process.
